results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 47 aligned units match their spec controlling ideas in spec order; the three callout entries (IN THIS CHAPTER, KEY POINTS, failure patterns) are the declared placements of the thesis statement and roadmap, not spec paragraphs. The p16 unit adds Stripe's KYC Refresh as further support for requirements becoming due without seller action.

results.draft_locus: How Verification Becomes Software: Requirements, Deadlines, Capabilities ¶3
results.finding: Marked two_ideas. One idea with support: how a Stripe requirement comes due and what a passed deadline does to the seller's money; the threshold and KYC Refresh sentences are routes into that same consequence, as the spec's controlling idea declares.

results.draft_locus: How Verification Becomes Software: Requirements, Deadlines, Capabilities ¶7
results.finding: Marked two_ideas. The webhook gap and the absence of a future_requirements counterpart are part of the spec's controlling idea (when Adyen re-verifies and how the platform learns of it); one idea with support, though the paragraph is dense.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim through its section (scene S2/S4, duties S1, state-model S2, monitoring S3, calendar S5, designs S4, comparison S2/S3, in-practice S4, failures S2/S4). The DORA paragraph traces to S5 only by its dated status, which the draft says openly.

Each table is framed by a sentence saying what it shows, each figure has an explanatory caption, and quotations are followed or preceded by their point (e.g. 'Part of each list is therefore risk appetite, not law'; 'A control that sat in the payment path now sits in account state, by law'; 'which is a provider's expectation, not law'). The 14/28-day Stripe cell and the FinCEN 2026 order are recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.draft_locus: Three Ways a Platform Can Hold Verification State ¶1
results.quote: A platform that embeds payments can respond to all this in three ways, which differ in what it stores.
results.finding: The declared problem_solution transition should pick up 'state that changes for reasons the seller and the platform do not control, on a calendar'; 'all this' names no known information, and coming straight after the PSD3 paragraph both flow readers felt the turn to the platform was abrupt.

All other declared transitions are expressed at their boundaries, e.g. 'The last four chapters were about the payer and the card' (contrast), 'A one-time "verified" flag cannot represent a loop' (cause_effect), 'Verification asks who the business is. Monitoring asks what it does' (contrast), 'The remaining items are to be tracked, not built' (contrast), 'Femke's team replayed the incident against the fields above' (example).

results.draft_locus: The Regulatory Calendar as of November 2026 ¶1
results.quote: Stripe's sentence about requirements changing "due to changes implemented by financial regulators" points at a calendar.
results.finding: Both readers could not see why the calendar sits between monitoring and the platform designs (reader 1: 'partly unclear'; reader 2: 'mostly unclear') and both proposed moving it later; it splits the run from provider state to platform design. The difficulty comes from the declared order (spec flow rationale places it here), not from the prose.
results.corroborated_by: flow reader 2, section 6 and item 7 (reader 1: section 6 and item 11)

results.draft_locus: The Regulatory Calendar as of November 2026 ¶2
results.quote: is on this calendar for its date and status only.
results.finding: Both readers stopped at a full paragraph the text itself says is off the chapter's subject and wondered why they were reading it. The spec declares the paragraph and its 'date and status only' role, so the fault is in the spec's content choice.

The does_not_know terms (KYC, KYB, obliged entity, beneficial owner, sanctions screening, PEP, transaction monitoring, financial intelligence unit, capability, requirement, deadline, DORA, instant payments, verification of payee, AML Regulation, PSD3/PSR) are each defined at or before their first use in running prose.
Opens on the puzzling scenario of 230 approved studios losing payouts, then bridges from the per-payment chapters; none of the weak patterns.

Sorted take-aways, the author's position, the part synthesis with a course of action, and the hand-off; it neither merely rephrases the thesis nor brings in new body evidence (the part-level claims come from earlier chapters of the part).

States what no section states (the five controls are one system, each returning a remainder that needs an owner) and why it matters (keep one table of what moved, what stayed and its owner instead of auditing certificates).
'Set the Card-Testing Weekend that opened the part beside the Frozen Studios ... 230 studios without payouts for up to 12 days' returns to the opening's 230 studios as the spec's callback requires.

The intro reader predicted all nine roadmap sections in order, the evidence (field-level documentation, the Larkfield case, a dated regulatory calendar, labeled inference) and the tone; only K6's content and the three designs were unknown, as expected.

The reader named a rule change with a passed deadline and a time/volume threshold (plus periodic review and compliance review), and listed stored requirements, deadlines and capability status, a named owner, a read channel, reminders and a daily sweep: the substance of the expected answer.

The reader gave timing (milliseconds on one payment vs days or weeks of behavior afterwards) and output (allow/block/challenge vs a case, confidential report or freeze the customer may not be told about), and that they share data but not a decision path.

The draft states 'Neither Stripe nor Adyen publishes its monitoring scenarios, its sanctions-screening logic or its re-verification intervals' and gives its account of the system in a callout headed 'INFERENCE, NOT DOCUMENTED', repeated in KEY POINTS and in the comparison table ('method not public').

The part closing connects the controls (card collection to fraud signals, portfolio fraud rate to exemptions, tokens and authentication to fees and disputes, identity data to account risk), sets the Card-Testing Weekend beside the Frozen Studios, and hands off to payments a clock starts for a billing period. The unnamed 'five controls' slowed both flow readers; that is recorded under flow_is_followable.
